about: Goldschmidt Vineyards belongs to Nick and Yolyn Goldschmidt, a husband-and-wife team from New Zealand who have lived in Healdsburg since 1990. Nick, who holds degrees in science, horticulture, viticulture and enology, joined Simi Winery in 1990 under Zelma Long and Paul Hobbs and became its chief winemaker a year later, before senior roles at Allied Domecq and Beam Estates. Today the family label follows his rule of “one vintage, one vineyard, one variety.”

Singing Tree is the family’s Chardonnay site, a historic hillside near Sebastopol in the cool western reaches of the Russian River Valley. The vines were planted in 1987 in sandy Gold Ridge loam, the fine, fast-draining soil of the old Wilson Grove Formation, and are cane-pruned on a U-shaped trellis. Nick keeps the oak in the background so the fruit and the site lead, using fermentation in steel and barrel with only partial malolactic conversion.

The winemaker describes melon, lemon, starfruit and a struck-flint, wet-stone note, with just a hint of nutmeg from the light touch of oak. It is a bright, mineral style of Russian River Chardonnay rather than a rich, buttery one, which makes it an easy partner for shellfish, roast chicken and vegetables from the wood fire.
facts: Gold Ridge sandy loam (Wilson Grove Formation)
